name: Marcus Brutus
description: A respected senator, Stoic philosopher, and friend of Caesar, descended from the Brutus who expelled Rome's last king. Persuaded that Caesar's ambition endangers the Republic, he joins the conspiracy and strikes the man he loves for the sake of an idea, then watches his cause unravel.

name: Caius Cassius
description: The lean, sharp-eyed senator who first organizes the conspiracy and recruits Brutus to lend it honor. Shrewd at reading other men's motives, he repeatedly defers to Brutus's worse judgment, and dies at Philippi on a misreading of the battle.

name: Julius Caesar
description: Rome's most powerful man, home in triumph and publicly offered a crown he three times refuses. Proud, superstitious yet dismissive of the omens that surround him, he is assassinated at the Capitol; his spirit then haunts the play and the conspirators to the end.

name: Mark Antony
description: Caesar's devoted friend, athlete, and a brilliant, unscrupulous orator. After the murder he secures safe conduct, then turns the Roman crowd against the conspirators with his funeral oration over Caesar's body, and joins the Triumvirate that destroys them.

name: Octavius Caesar
description: Caesar's young great-nephew and named heir, who arrives in Rome to claim his place. Cold, composed, and quietly assertive, he forms the Second Triumvirate with Antony and Lepidus and shares command of the victorious army at Philippi.

name: Lepidus
description: The third member of the ruling Triumvirate, used by Antony to mark off the men to be killed in the proscriptions. Antony dismisses him to Octavius as a 'slight, unmeritable man, meet to be sent on errands.'

name: Casca
description: A blunt, sardonic senator who gives the sour eyewitness account of Caesar refusing the crown and of Cicero speaking Greek. Unnerved by the night's prodigies, he strikes the first blow against Caesar.

name: Decius Brutus
description: The conspirator who promises he can flatter Caesar to the Capitol, reinterpreting Calpurnia's bloody dream as a vision of Rome's renewal and playing on Caesar's vanity about the crown.

name: Cinna
description: A conspirator who helps Cassius win Brutus over, planting forged petitions where Brutus will find them. (This edition gives the same speech-prefix to Cinna the poet, who is torn apart by the mob in Act 3.)

name: Metellus Cimber
description: The conspirator whose suit to recall his banished brother gives the assassins their pretext to press around Caesar at the Capitol.

name: Trebonius
description: The conspirator who draws Mark Antony out of the way while the others kill Caesar, sparing Antony at Brutus's insistence.

name: Caius Ligarius
description: A sick senator who throws off his illness to follow Brutus, whom he reveres, into the conspiracy.

name: Calpurnia
description: Caesar's wife, whose nightmare of his statue running blood and whose dread of the day's omens nearly keep him home. Decius's flattery overrides her warning, and Caesar goes to his death.

name: Portia
description: Brutus's wife and the daughter of Cato. Stoic and strong-willed, she gives herself a voluntary wound in the thigh to prove she can be trusted with his secret; in his absence she dies by swallowing fire.

name: Soothsayer
description: The seer who calls out of the crowd to 'beware the ides of March,' and meets Caesar again on the day itself to warn that the ides are come but not gone.

name: Artemidorus
description: A teacher of rhetoric who writes Caesar a letter naming the conspirators and tries, too late, to press it on him on the way to the Capitol.

name: Cicero
description: A famous senator and orator who comments wryly on the storm and speaks Greek at the games. The conspirators consider and reject recruiting him; he is later killed in the proscriptions.

name: Publius
description: An elderly senator who comes with the others to escort Caesar and is left stunned and trembling in the aftermath of the assassination.

name: Popilius Lena
description: A senator who terrifies Cassius moments before the killing by wishing that his 'enterprise today may thrive,' seeming for an instant to have betrayed the plot.

name: Flavius
description: A tribune who, with Marullus, scolds the commoners for celebrating Caesar's triumph and strips the festival decorations from his statues; the two are later 'put to silence.'

name: Marullus
description: A tribune who rebukes the fickle crowd for cheering Caesar when they had once loved Pompey, whom Caesar has just defeated.

name: Lucius
description: Brutus's young servant boy, gentle and loyal, who plays the lute for his sleepless master and dozes over the instrument on the eve of Philippi.

name: Lucilius
description: An officer loyal to Brutus who, captured at Philippi, claims to be Brutus to protect him and is spared by an admiring Antony.

name: Titinius
description: Cassius's trusted officer and friend. Mistakenly reported captured, he is the cause of Cassius's despairing suicide, and kills himself with Cassius's sword beside the body.

name: Messala
description: An officer in the republican army who reports the proscriptions and Portia's death, and who finds Cassius dead on the field at Philippi.

name: Pindarus
description: Cassius's bondman, brought from Parthia. At Cassius's order he runs him through with his own sword, then flees to freedom.

name: Varro
description: A servant of Brutus who sleeps in his tent the night the Ghost appears before Philippi.

name: Claudius
description: A servant of Brutus who, with Varro, lies in his master's tent on the night of the Ghost; not to be confused with the king in Hamlet.

name: Clitus
description: A follower of Brutus at Philippi who refuses, like the others, to hold the sword for his master's suicide.

name: Dardanius
description: A follower of Brutus who, like Clitus, cannot bring himself to kill his master when asked.

name: Volumnius
description: An old schoolfellow of Brutus who declines his friend's quiet request to hold the sword on which Brutus means to die.

name: Strato
description: The follower who at last holds the sword steady so that Brutus can run upon it, then enters Octavius's service.

name: Young Cato
description: Son of Marcus Cato and brother of Portia, who proclaims his name aloud and is killed fighting in the republican cause at Philippi.

name: Ghost of Caesar
description: The spirit of the murdered Caesar, who appears to Brutus in his tent before Philippi as his 'evil spirit' and promises to meet him on the battlefield.

name: First Citizen
description: A commoner of Rome. In Act 1 a carpenter rebuked by the tribunes; in Act 3 one of the plebeians swayed back and forth by Brutus's and Antony's funeral speeches.

name: Second Citizen
description: A commoner of Rome. In Act 1 the quick-witted cobbler who jokes with the tribunes; in Act 3 a plebeian moved by Antony to mutiny.

name: Third Citizen
description: One of the Roman plebeians who hear the funeral orations and turn against the conspirators.

name: Fourth Citizen
description: One of the Roman plebeians at Caesar's funeral, roused by Antony's reading of the will.

name: Citizens
description: The Roman crowd speaking as one, by turns cheering the conspirators and then howling for their blood after Antony's oration.

name: First Soldier
description: A soldier in the armies at Philippi.

name: Second Soldier
description: A soldier in the armies at Philippi.

name: Third Soldier
description: A soldier in the armies at Philippi.

name: Messenger
description: A messenger who reports the approach of the enemy army to the field at Philippi.

name: Poet
description: A self-appointed peacemaker who bursts into the generals' tent to reconcile the quarreling Brutus and Cassius, and is mocked out again.

name: Servant
description: One of several servants who carry messages between their masters — Caesar, Antony, and Octavius — at the play's turning points.
